obs_mark_001_pattern.name: Titration Peak / Wax-Wane / Efficacy Decay Tradeoff
obs_mark_001_pattern.validation_status: Mark canonical clinical pattern (validated observation, under Mark's observational authority)

description.1_titration_peak_phase: При каждом повышении дозы (0.25 → 0.5 → 1.0 → 2.0 mg) — резкое усиление всех побочных эффектов одновременно: nausea, GI discomfort, иногда vomiting, taste changes.
description.2_adaptation_phase_wax_wane: За 2-4 недели побочные эффекты постепенно снижаются. Пациент достигает relative tolerability.
description.3_critical_observation: Одновременно со снижением побочек снижается и терапевтический эффект. Адаптация — это не только GI tolerance, но и attenuation of intended pharmacological action (appetite, gastric emptying).
description.4_late_phase_constipation: После того как nausea/vomiting проходят, constipation становится доминирующей побочкой — контраст с ранней фазой (nausea/diarrhea).

clinical_dilemma_mark_canonical: Higher doses = more side effects, but also more therapeutic effect
Lower doses = better tolerance, but inadequate clinical impact
Time-stable middle dose: tolerability good but efficacy attenuated
Need to find personalized sweet spot, varies by patient.

cholestyramine_for_constipation.hypothesis: Mark гипотезирует, что cholestyramine (anion exchange resin) может быть полезен в late-phase constipation. Mechanism rationale: bile acid binding → может modulate GLP-1-induced bile acid changes, или просто improve stool consistency через alternative pathway.

prolongation_of_therapeutic_effect.hypothesis: Как избежать adaptation/attenuation? Возможные strategies (все гипотетические): dose holidays/drug rotation; combination с agents через различные mechanisms; cyclical dosing patterns; adjustment of food intake patterns to maintain GI signal.
prolongation_of_therapeutic_effect.status: emerging research area, no validated protocols yet

literature_check_rf._note: [RF] Literature scan (Jun-2026) in response to Mark's 4 questions. Research evidence only — does NOT change mark_validated (stays PARTIAL), does NOT operationalize any hypothesis into clinical guidance, does NOT lift any flag. Hypotheses remain physician-owned.

q1_wax_wane_pattern_confirmed.gastric_emptying_satiety_axis: [RCT/preclinical] Tachyphylaxis of GLP-1-induced gastric-emptying delay is documented (Nauck). Rat study: long-acting liraglutide gastric-emptying delay diminished within ~14 days, short-acting exenatide sustained (Diabetes 2014). Human: liraglutide 3 mg gastric half-emptying markedly prolonged at 5 weeks but significantly less at 16 weeks (Halawi, Lancet Gastroenterol Hepatol 2017). → Mark's wax-wane of GI effect is literature-backed for the gastric-emptying/satiety-signal axis.
q1_wax_wane_pattern_confirmed.weight_axis_caveat: [GL] Weight-loss efficacy does NOT classically show early receptor-tachyphylaxis plateau — STEP/SUSTAIN trials show ongoing loss to ~60-68 weeks. Late weight plateau is attributed mainly to metabolic adaptation + appetite-circuit re-equilibration, not receptor desensitization. → The 'efficacy decays as side-effects wane' coupling is real for the GI/satiety signal but should not be conflated wholesale with weight-loss attenuation.

q2_cholestyramine_for_constipation.verdict: [RF] NO published support; mechanistically questionable for constipation.
findings: [CLASS] Cholestyramine (bile acid sequestrant) itself commonly CAUSES constipation — using it to treat GLP-1-induced constipation is mechanistically backwards.

[RCT] The published GLP-1↔bile-acid data runs the opposite direction: GLP-1RAs are used/studied to TREAT bile-acid DIARRHEA (liraglutide; JCEM Case Reports luac004 2023; once-weekly sema vs once-daily lira on BAD, PMC10578406) — consistent with GLP-1 reducing bile-acid-driven colonic secretion/transit, i.e. contributing to constipation, not relieving it.
[GL] Evidence-based management of GLP-1 constipation = osmotic laxative (PEG 3350), fiber, hydration, slower titration.
q2_cholestyramine_for_constipation.status_for_mark: Hypothesis remains UNTESTED and now flagged as mechanistically counter-indicated by the bile-acid literature. Physician decision — recorded, not endorsed.

findings: [GL] Drug holidays / cyclical dosing: no validated protocol; cessation → weight regain in systematic review + nonlinear meta-regression (ScienceDirect 2026), arguing AGAINST holidays.

[GL] Evidence-based plateau responses: dose escalation to max (sema 2.4 mg; Wegovy HD 7.2 mg FDA-approved Mar 2026); switch to dual GIP/GLP-1 tirzepatide; resistance training + protein for lean mass; sleep/stress optimization.
[RF] G-protein-biased agonism (less β-arrestin recruitment/desensitization) — preclinical/experimental only.

q4_agent_differences.verdict: [RF] YES — half-life / dosing frequency drives the GI-tachyphylaxis differential.
findings: [RCT] GI-effect tachyphylaxis is contingent on sustained ~24h receptor exposure → long-acting once-weekly semaglutide shows MORE gastric-emptying tachyphylaxis (faster GI wax-wane) than shorter-acting agents (daily liraglutide, BID exenatide) — consistent with Mark observing it specifically on semaglutide.
[RCT] Constipation signal: semaglutide highest among GLP-1RAs in FAERS disproportionality (ROR ~6.17, PMC9770009).
[CLASS] Tirzepatide (GIP/GLP-1): greater weight efficacy; GI AE profile broadly class-similar; dedicated wax-wane comparison data limited.
